An evaluation of the mineral ownership other than coal was made by Douglas Freeman, Attorney at Law for Westmoreland Resources in the spring of 1975. He determined that there were 65 individual owners of minerals exclusive of coal in Tract III. It is assumed that Tract II ownership would be similar.
Tract III originally had 18 different surface owners, but Westmore-land Resources has been acquiring title to the surface. Resistance to sale of the private lands was very strong until late 1975, however, landowners have remained and are ranching or farming lands on a lease basis with Westmoreland Resources. Only four surface owners remain in Tract III which Westmoreland has not bought out. The largest block of surface ownership not yet purchased is the southern portion of Tract III and comprises approximately three sections. Westmoreland has indicated they plan to purchase all remaining surface ownership in both Tracts II and III as needed for mining. The strength of this intent is evidenced by Westmoreland Resources success in obtaining their current holdings.
In addition to the 30,876 acres included in the Crow Leases, West-moreland Resources has leased 2,560 acres of State lands and 1,962 acres of adjacent privately owned coal rights.
